OBJECTIVE 1.1 Development Objective Original Development Objective (Approved as part of Approval package on 24-Feb-2020) The objectives of the Project are to: (a) improve passenger ferry infrastructure and service in Assam, and (b) improve the institutional capacity and framework for inland water transport in Assam Has the Development Objective been changed since Board Approval of the Project Objective? KEY ISSUES & STATUS 4.1 Implementation Status and Key Decisions The construction of the Guwahati Gateway Ghat is complete and was inaugurated on November 7, 2025. Construction activities at the three ferry terminals—Umananda, Neamati, and Aphalamukh—resumed in September 2025 and are progressing. Installation of two floating HDPE jetties at Rajaduar and Kamalabari has been finalized. Activities under Component 1 (Institutional, regulatory, and safety strengthening) and Component 2 (Fleet safety improvements and modernization) are advancing as planned and are expected to be completed by November 2026. 5. KEY ISSUES & STATUS 4.1 Implementation Status and Key Decisions Sep 11, 2025 Page 1 of 20 The World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report Assam Inland Water Transport Project (P157929) Construction of the Guwahati Gateway Ghat is almost completed.

Construction at the 3 ferry terminals at Umananda, Neamati and Aphalamukh have been delayed due to revision of technical designs, with construction now expected to resume in September 2025. The construction at the North Guwahati terminal has been foreclosed in light of concerns regarding its alleged impacts on the adjacent bridge under construction. Installation of 2 floating HDPE jetties at Rajaduar and Kamalabari is close to completion. Activities under Component 1 (Institutional, regulatory and safety strengthening) and 2 (Fleet safety improvements and modernization) are on track for completion by December 2025. 5. KEY ISSUES & STATUS Apr 11, 2025 Page 1 of 20 The World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report Assam Inland Water Transport Project (P157929) 4.1 Implementation Status and Key Decisions The construction of the Guwahati terminal is 98% complete and is expected to be completed by April 2025. Civil works construction at the 3 ferry terminals at Umananda, Neamati and Aphalamukh have been delayed due to revision of technical designs and are now planned for completion in November 2025. The construction at the North Guwahati terminal has been put on hold due concerns on its possible impacts on the nearby bridge under construction and suitable steps to ensure continuity of ferry services between the new Guwahati terminal to North Guwahati area are being reviewed. The installation of 2 floating HDPE jetties at Rajaduar and Kamalabari and a new vessel crew training centre at Guwahati (Pandu) are expected to be completed by November 2025. The project completion date was extended to December 31, 2025 to complete the outstanding activities. 5. KEY ISSUES & STATUS Sep 23, 2024 Page 1 of 18 The World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report Assam Inland Water Transport Project (P157929) 4.1 Implementation Status and Key Decisions Project implementation has progressed substantially. Twenty new and modern vessels were procured and are already deployed for IWT services in Assam. The main passenger ferry terminal at Guwahati is expected to be ready for operations in November 2024, four smaller terminals are under construction, and two smaller modular jetties are under procurement. Night navigation facilities / virtual navigations aids are deployed on two out of three high traffic routes and almost 810 small boats are upgraded to enhance safety. Importantly, two new independent agencies for improved service delivery and regulations are established and functional. Project extension is under discussion as the monsoon flooding has delayed the completion of civil works by five months. 5. ctory Overall Risk Rating Substantial Substantial Implementation Status and Key Decisions The project implementation has progressed well across all activities including civil works (commenced in December 2024) at four smaller terminals: North- Guwahati, Umananda, Neamati and Aphalamukh ferry terminals. A new fleet of 20 Catamaran vessels, 3 Tugboats and 3 Search and Rescue vessels are deployed for operations in Guwahati, Jorhat and Dhubri divisions to augment inland water transportation and passenger services in Assam. The night navigation system operational in Guwahati has been extended on the Neamati – Aphalamukh route as well in March 2024. The Assam Inland Water Transport Regulatory Authority has adopted the National Inland Vessel Rules framed under the IV Act 2021 and published the Safety and Economic regulations. Training was provided to 2600 IWT staff and 1600 private vessel operators and 712 marine engines were provided under the Jibondinga incentive scheme to country boat operators, along with life buoys and life jackets, to enhance safety. Together with the infrastructure investments, it enables safe, efficient, and sustainable ferry operations and passenger services.

tory Overall Risk Rating Substantial Substantial Implementation Status and Key Decisions The project implementation has progressed, but would require close monitoring to avoid delays in completion next year. The civil works tender process for the development of the four smaller ferry terminals (two terminals each in the Guwahati cluster and Majuli cluster) was concluded and is expected to be awarded during October 2023. The second lot of 10 new Catamaran vessels, 3 Tugboats and a Search and Rescue vessel were launched for operations and would enhance inland water transportation and passenger services in Assam. The night navigation system is operational in Guwahati facilitating ferry service operations after daylight hours, and will be extended to cover selected routes at Majuli and Dhubri by January 2024. The Assam Inland Water Transport Regulatory Authority has adopted the National Inland Vessel Rules framed under the IV Act 2021 and published the Safety regulations. The Economic regulations are being drafted and expected to be adopted by November 2023. Together with the infrastructure investments, it enables safe, efficient and sustainable ferry operations and passenger services.

al Substantial Implementation Status and Key Decisions The overall implementation progress is moderately satisfactory. The Chairperson at the Assam Inland Water Transport Regulatory Authority (RA) is recently appointed and developing the institutional capacity is critical to implement safety and sector development reforms. The asset management and operating companies - Assam Shipping Company and Assam Port Company that are being established also need to be functional at earliest to ensure the safe and efficient operations of the new vessels that are being delivered and the ferry terminals that are planned for development. Three new ferry vessels with 100 passenger capacity, were commissioned for operations on the main ferry routes in Assam on 17th September 2021. The construction of the remaining 17 vessels have been delayed due to the pandemic and is expected to be delivered during the next 12 months. The initial procurement of 2600 lifejackets and 500 lifebuoys for passenger boats as well as 3 man-overboard rescue boats were delivered and have been deployed at Guwahati and Majuli to enhance safety and emergency response services. The retrofitting and upgrading of 10/6/2021 Page 1 of 9 The World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report Assam Inland Water Transport Project (P157929) 7 vessels are ongoing, including fixtures for special needs passengers and fauna friendly devices.

As part of the incentive scheme (Jibondinga) targeted to improve the condition and safety of country boats, 157 vessels are identified to be retrofitted as on 16th Sept ‘21. The DPR for the ferry terminal at Aphalamukh ghat in Majuli is being reviewed based on the revised traffic flows, while the civil works contract for the construction of the Guwahati Gateway Ghat is expected to proceed after the evaluation of bids received. Feasibilities studies and project reports for the remaining ferry terminals planned under the project are being prepared. A multi-country team of World Wildlife Fund has submitted the report on Conservation of Gangetic Dolphin covering Brahmaputra and Ganga river main stems and the final report will be launched after the regional stakeholder workshop that is delayed due to the pandemic. The dolphin study will inform the Environmental Assessment for the new activities, and the revision to the Cumulative Impact Assessment for the project.

mentation Status and Key Decisions The overall implementation progress is moderately satisfactory. The Project Implementation Unit (PIU) has engaged a project manager and additional technical staff are expected to join to enhance project implementation. The delivery schedules of new ferry vessels have been delayed due to the pandemic and would be phased into the IWT services by December 2021. The retrofitting and upgrading of the vessels operated by DIWTA is being scheduled in smaller lots, without disruptions to service. The specifications for new vessels include the provision for fauna friendly devices - improved propeller design with propeller guards as well as acoustic 'pingers' that repel dolphins approaching the vessels. Many private vessel operators including women entrepreneurs and unregistered boat operators have applied to avail the benefits of the incentive scheme (Jibondinga), targeted to improve the condition and safety of country boats. The PIU conducted meetings to raise general awareness about 2/1/2021 Page 1 of 10 The World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report Assam Inland Water Transport Project (P157929) the scheme and has developed a well-documented and approved process to support the first phase of implementation. Specific training on environment friendly operations of boats being improved through the scheme is included in the implementation plan.

The ferry terminal design for Aphalamukh ghat in Majuli has received clearance from national waterway authority, however the procurement of civil works contractor is being held back since the national Ministry of Road Transport and Highway has invited proposals for construction of a new bridge over Brahmaputra river, near to the location of the ferry terminal. The project will review the terminal design and location based on the revised traffic forecast at Majuli, while fast tracking the priority development works at other locations including Guwahati. Bid documents for proposed Works Contracts include specific requirements of: timing of construction to avoid important periods in Dolphin life cycle; requirement of equipment like bubble screens for in-water construction; additional ecological expertise in contractor team; and 2% performance guarantee for Environment, Health, Safety, and Social (ESHS) aspects. The Cumulative Impact Assessment (CIA) prepared at the appraisal of the project is being revised and would be finalized prior to the award of the ferry terminal works contracts. The project would benefit from the multi-country study on Gangetic Dolphins that is commissioned by the Bank. The study for dolphin sensitive development is reviewing global best practices for effective and sustainable conservation of freshwater dolphins and to help identify and build support for appropriate mitigation measures for protection of Gangetic Dolphin.

A multi-country team of World Wildlife Fund is working on this study covering Brahmaputra and Ganga river main stems and the final report is expected to be available by July 2021.
